learningObjectives.title: The composition and evolution of the Earth's atmosphere
Carbon dioxide and methane as greenhouse gases
Common atmospheric pollutants and their sources

questions.q: Which gas makes up about four fifths of the Earth's atmosphere today?
questions.explain: Nitrogen makes up approximately 80% (about four fifths) of today's atmosphere.

questions.q: Approximately what proportion of the Earth's present atmosphere is oxygen?
questions.explain: Oxygen makes up about 20% (roughly one fifth) of the modern atmosphere.

questions.q: For approximately how long have the proportions of gases in the atmosphere been more or less as they are today?
questions.explain: The proportions of atmospheric gases have been roughly constant for about the last 200 million years.

questions.q: The Earth's early atmosphere is thought to have consisted mainly of which gas?
questions.explain: The early atmosphere is thought to have been mainly carbon dioxide, similar to the atmospheres of Mars and Venus today.

questions.q: What is thought to have released most of the gases that formed the Earth's early atmosphere?
questions.explain: Intense volcanic activity during the first billion years released gases such as carbon dioxide, water vapour, nitrogen, methane and ammonia.

questions.q: How are the Earth's oceans thought to have formed?
options: Water vapour in the atmosphere condensed as the Earth cooled
Oxygen reacted with hydrogen locked in rocks
The polar ice caps melted and spread
questions.explain: As the Earth cooled, water vapour released by volcanoes condensed to form the oceans.

questions.q: Which organisms are thought to have first produced oxygen in the Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explain: Algae first produced oxygen by photosynthesis about 2.7 billion years ago, before green plants evolved.

questions.q: Which process removed large amounts of carbon dioxide from the early atmosphere?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis by algae and plants used up carbon dioxide, and much was also dissolved in the oceans and locked into sediments and fossil fuels.

questions.q: Which balanced equation correctly represents photosynthesis?
questions.explain: In photosynthesis carbon dioxide and water are converted into glucose and oxygen using light energy.

questions.q: Which of the following is a list of greenhouse gases?
options: Carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour
Carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide and soot
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour are the greenhouse gases that help maintain temperatures on Earth.

questions.q: How do greenhouse gases help to keep the Earth warm?
options: They absorb long wavelength (infrared) radiation re-emitted from the Earth's surface
They reflect all incoming sunlight back to the surface
They release heat through chemical reactions in the air
They trap oxygen close to the ground
questions.explain: Greenhouse gases absorb the long wavelength infrared radiation re-radiated by the Earth and release energy that keeps the atmosphere warm.

questions.q: Which human activity is a major source of the greenhouse gas methane?
questions.explain: Agriculture, including cattle farming and rice fields, along with decomposing waste in landfill, releases large amounts of methane.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of methane?
questions.explain: Methane has the formula CH4, with one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms.

questions.q: A country greatly increases the amount of coal and oil burned in its power stations. Which greenhouse gas will most directly increase as a result?
questions.explain: Burning fossil fuels such as coal and oil releases carbon dioxide, increasing its concentration in the atmosphere.

questions.q: Which statement best describes carbon monoxide?
options: A toxic, colourless and odourless gas
A pungent gas that causes acid rain
A green gas used in photosynthesis
A solid particulate that causes global dimming
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide is toxic, colourless and odourless, making it difficult to detect.

questions.q: Carbon monoxide is produced when a fuel undergoes which process?
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide forms during incomplete combustion, when there is not enough oxygen to fully oxidise the carbon to carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Which pollutant, released from sulfur impurities in fuels, is a major cause of acid rain?
questions.explain: Sulfur dioxide is produced when sulfur impurities in fuels burn, and it causes acid rain and respiratory problems.

questions.q: How are oxides of nitrogen produced inside a car engine?
options: Nitrogen and oxygen react together at the high temperatures inside the engine
Nitrogen present in the fuel is oxidised
questions.explain: The high temperatures inside engines cause nitrogen and oxygen from the air to react, forming oxides of nitrogen.

questions.q: Particulates (soot and unburnt hydrocarbons) released into the air can cause which problems?
options: Acid rain and corrosion of metals
questions.explain: Particulates cause global dimming by reflecting sunlight and can damage the lungs, causing respiratory problems.

questions.q: A gas boiler burns natural gas in a poorly ventilated room, producing a toxic gas that binds to haemoglobin and prevents the blood carrying oxygen. Which gas is this?
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide from incomplete combustion binds to haemoglobin, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
